commentary_title: Rising cargo activity supports aframax fleet emplyment
commentary_summary: Aframax utilisation declined 1.1 percentage points WoW, yet remained 0.3 percentage point above MoM and 1.5 percentage points YoY, while the tonne-mile index rose to 104, up 2.6% YoY. The combination of firmer utilisation and improving tonne-mile demand points to resilient crude trade activity, helping sustain fleet employment. | Cargo absorption strengthened across both regions, with the share of laden vessels increasing by 6.5 percentage points MoM in the east and 3.2 percentage points in the west. Rising anchored capacity in the west and stable levels in the east suggest greater vessel engagement in cargo operations, while elevated laden tonnage at anchor across the Atlantic and Pacific indicates support from regional crude movements. | Market tightness remained broadly balanced as stronger cargo activity was partly offset by improving productivity. Faster vessel repositioning continued to support effective fleet supply, limiting upward pressure on freight rates despite healthy utilisation levels.
